hard_rejections: A candidate gives an incorrect final answer on any evaluated item that matched native answers correctly.
A candidate fails to complete an item that matched native completes correctly.
Any executable correctness, cache lifecycle, graph replay, retained-score, source-handoff or memory gate fails.
A tested benchmark, domain or workload regresses in observed quality.
A required correctness or performance workload is omitted from the report.
answer_judges: Independent benchmark keys and executable tests; native output is not assumed optimal. Thinking text may diverge.
selection_proxy: Diagnostic only. Native-key recall never substitutes for final-answer quality.

required_coverage.scope: Frozen independent contexts across all six domains and short/long strata; pilot and calibration remain separate.
All 164 tasks under pinned base and extended executable tests; final code only; isolated execution.
Pinned public benchmark with independent generated answer keys through the supported context envelope; integration pending.
Code and prose; concurrency 1,2,4 and normal load; cold and cached short/32K/64K/long contexts; mixed prefills, admission, memory and request failures.
Fixed task scope and tool policy; completed correct findings and elapsed time; server telemetry recorded.

speed_gate: Two fresh candidate boots; matched controls or immutable compatible references; uncertainty per workload; lower confidence bound for a speed ratio must exceed one before calling a workload a win. No claim of universal victory from finite tests.
runtime_costs: Required construction and updates remain timed. Reference scoring, grading, training, proofs, host captures and duplicate validation remain out of band.
promotion: Unqualified until every required gate passes and the owner accepts the candidate. No configuration or immutable baseline changes in this experiment.
